evidence.note: Identified that stock evaluate.py used the wrong role_colon renderer + HF tokenizer, and built a custom my_eval.py using the llama3 renderer consistent with training; tested it manually before use. Real verification-harness design.

auto_eval.py re-evaluates every checkpoint and only updates best_checkpoint.txt/best_score.txt on a measured improvement — every 'new best' is backed by a real re-measured IFEval score, not a loss curve.
Confirms scoring runs on the full 541 IFEval samples (adequate sample size, not a one-off), though it never reproduced the ~26% base-model baseline to validate the harness.

Noted 'Variance is high' but never quantified noise or used determinism; final reported 48.06% is the max across many noisy per-checkpoint evals with no confirmatory re-measurement of the selected best — max-selection bias unaddressed.

reasoning: The agent built a genuinely working IFEval harness, correctly fixing the renderer mismatch to match training and scoring on the full 541-sample set, and gated every best_checkpoint update on a real re-measured score — clearly above anchor 3's 'unverified renderer / noisy one-off' description. But it never reproduced the ~26% baseline to validate the harness (the core of anchor 5) and never accounted for sampling noise (anchor 8), instead reporting the max of many noisy checkpoint evals without a confirmatory re-eval. This places it at anchor 5: a trustworthy, re-used eval that gates improvements, but missing baseline reproduction and noise handling.
